audit.why: 50.92% over 5100 games. Ahri owns level 1 on range, levels 2-6 are a positioning skill check against the vault, two items goes back to Ahri. Matches packet.levelChart.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere (packet defect: sequencingCues 0). Rake 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, Noxian Diplomacy 8 -> 6s, Shadow Assault 100/80/60, Assassin's Path 0s but with a long per-wall lockout.
audit.why: The per-wall lockout is the real spike gate: a wall he has already used is not available for the next engage.
audit.corrected: Numbers and the wall lockout written into breakdown.cooldowns and wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Text calls it a 'W-E wall-vault combo' (whys[1], spikes[0], wants.foe[0]) — the vault is Assassin's Path (E); W is Rake. Two decisive mechanics were absent: Assassin's Path has no cooldown but puts the used terrain on a long one, and Blade's End needs three Wound stacks plus an autoattack before the bleed lands. Charm stopping movement abilities cancels both the vault and the Q leap and is never stated.
audit.why: Riot text: E 'vaults over any terrain... low cooldown, but puts the used terrain on a long cooldown'; Q 'if they are outside melee range, Talon will leap at his target'; Ahri E 'instantly stopping movement abilities'.
audit.corrected: Named the vault correctly, added the terrain lockout, the Wound bleed, and charm-cancels-the-leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed across layers on rows 1 and 7: win[0] and win[6] read 'Ahri' while phases[0].side and phases[6].side read 'Skill'.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side and phases[6].side flipped to Ahri; the middle five already agree at 'Skill'.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Count it out loud if you must. - Your R Spirit Rush (last dash) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Rake is 9s at rank 1 and the return blades carry the damage and the slow — stand off the return line. - Assassin's Path has no cooldown, but each wall he vaults goes down for a long time, so the one he just used is closed. - Charm cancels both the vault and the Q leap.

edits.before: His W-E wall-vault combo can burst you down once he's ahead in levels, making good positioning near river walls a genuine skill check.
edits.after: His pattern is Assassin's Path over the wall into Rake and a Q leap from 575 — position so the wall he can use is behind you, not beside.

edits.before: Talon's W-E combo lets him vault a wall and burst you down fast once he's ahead in levels, so this is a genuine skill window where good positioning away from the river wall and tracking his cooldowns keeps you safe.
edits.after: Talon vaults a wall with Assassin's Path into Rake and a Q leap, and three spells plus one auto sets off his Wound bleed — the skill window is standing where no unused wall reaches you and charming the leap.

edits.before: Vault the river wall with W-E to open an unexpected burst combo
edits.after: Vault an unused wall with Assassin's Path to open the burst

edits.before: Ward the river wall and avoid standing near jungle entrances he can vault from
edits.after: Track which walls he has already vaulted — each one is shut for a while

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Talon wins by vaulting a wall you did not watch, stacking Wound with Rake and Q, and killing you with the bleed.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — charm him mid-vault and he arrives next to you with no dash left and no Wound stacked.

edits.before: Talon spends Rake early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Noxian Diplomacy leaps only from range — its 575 is his real threat radius.

edits.before: That is Talon’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Charm is your only answer to his vault — without it you're free.

edits.before: If Talon gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Rake extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through charm picks.
edits.after: If Talon gets a kill his Wound bleed starts one-shotting you through the wave — hold charm and farm at max orb range. Two kills: Q-clear, ward both walls, and take your picks elsewhere.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Talon's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, shove with Q and roam: Assassin's Path lets him do the same, so beat him to it and charm the lane he was heading for.

notes: Two mechanics that decide this lane were absent from every field: Assassin's Path having no cooldown but locking out the wall it used, and Blade's End needing three Wound stacks plus an autoattack. The 'W-E wall-vault' phrasing mis-slotted the vault. suspectNames flagged 'Use Shadow Assault' and 'Shadow Assault's' — both FALSE POSITIVES, that is the correct R name. Did not assert whether charm reveals him inside Shadow Assault's invisibility or whether the bleed can be cleansed — not in the kit text.
